sections.title: The Iranian Nuclear Program: History, Science, Politics
sections.description: Since the late 1990s, Iran’s nuclear program has been a source of controversy, challenge and – often – confusion. Successive US administrations, in concert with close allies in the Middle East and elsewhere, have vowed to do everything possible to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. However, away from the media hype and the political machinations, there has not always been a clear understanding of Iran’s nuclear intentions and strategies. This course examines Iran’s controversial nuclear program from three critical perspectives: history, science and politics. Students will come to understand the importance of viewing Iran’s nuclear program through the prism of history – from its origins under the Shah’s regime in the 1950s, to the close US-Iranian nuclear cooperation of the 1960s and 1970s, to the changing dynamic that followed the Iranian revolution in the 1980s and 1990s. Students will also develop a rudimentary appreciation of nuclear physics and the role that nuclear technology has played in the economic and political agendas of developing countries since the Second World War. Finally, students will learn to approach the politics of this issue with a critical lens – subjecting the many different claims made by Iran and its adversaries to scrutiny and analysis, and appreciating the ways this issue intersects with broader geopolitical issues, most significantly the fraught relationship between Iran and the United States.
